name: Pye Krumen
world_status: statement found in an open source

new_statements.quote: [p.4] Phonology: There is a tendency towards monosyllabism. The preferred syllable structures are V, CV or CLV. A given syllable is either oral or nasalized and is characterized by tone (H, M, La, Lb, LbH). Tepo/Plapo have 9 vowels, Piè has 12. [...] [p.6] The Krumen languages are tone languages [...] The Krumen cluster – Tepo, Plapo and Piè – fits the general picture of the Kru languages: All three languages are characterized by a three-level tone system – high / mid / low [...] Each syllable of a given word is a potential tone bearing unit TBU
new_statements.citation: Thalmann, Peter. 2026. Tonal puzzles in 3 Krumen languages (SW of Côte d'Ivoire): phonological, grammatical and historical issues. SIL ms., 3rd revised version, 40 pp. (kroumen.com)
new_statements.locator: sec. 1.4 'Language features', p. 4; sec. 2.1 'Tone inventory', p. 6
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened (extracted text pp. 4-6). Sec. 1.4 'Language features', p. 4 reads exactly: 'Phonology: There is a tendency towards monosyllabism. The preferred syllable structures are V, CV or CLV. A given syllable is either oral or nasalized and is characterized by tone (H, M, La, Lb, LbH). Tepo/Plapo have 9 vowels, Piè has 12.' Sec. 2.1 'Tone inventory: four tonemes (H, M, La, Lb) on three levels', p. 6 reads: 'The Krumen languages are tone languages... The Krumen cluster – Tepo, Plapo and Piè – fits the general picture of the Kru languages: All three languages are characterized by a three-level tone system – high / mid / low... Each syllable of a given word is a potential tone bearing unit TBU'.…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Piè Krumen is described as a three-level tone language (tonemes H, M, La, Lb, plus LbH) in which every syllable bears a tone; the source (and the Piè-specific SIL orthography guide of 2015) says nothing about word stress or accent.
new_statements.exceptions: none; the only 'accent' mentions refer to orthographic tone diacritics
new_statements.domain_note: Statement concerns lexical tone on the syllable/word; no word- or phrase-level stress discussed.
new_statements.identity_note: Thalmann's tone papers treat Piè [pye] ('Bereby Kru', Grand-Béréby to San Pedro) alongside Tepo [ted] and Plapo [ktj]; the quoted statements are explicitly asserted for all three, with Piè-specific details (12 vowels, no Lb spreading). The 2015 SIL guide is Piè-specific (pyek1235). The fuller grammar (Thalmann 2023/1987) and Phonologie du kroumen (1980) describe Tepo (tepo1239), not Piè.
